Find a project that fits you
Not sure where to start? Explore resources on AI tools, content and digital products. See what each project involves and which skills it needs, then choose a starting point.
Follow clear steps to start a project
Once you choose a direction, follow hands-on guides and tasks, with live explanations and Q&A. Shengcai calls these project training programs “Voyages”.
Meet in person to discuss choosing a direction, finding customers and solving problems. Bring your own questions and choose an event that fits your city and schedule.
Use AI to think through your questions

Tell the AI assistant your project idea or question. It draws on the community’s project experience to help you think through your options and next steps. Ask it when you are choosing a direction or stuck on a specific task.
How do members use the community?
Explore how members start projects, work through obstacles and describe their experience in the community.
12 selected stories · Scroll sideways for more
Some have found a path; others are still exploring
Xiaoxia values a community willing to try new things. Members share methods and ask questions, turning exchanges of information into connections and friendships.
Make a complex idea small enough to launch
Yinhe Xingyou began with an interactive novel that kept growing in scope. Switching to a simpler AI puzzle game helped them launch a website, add payments and reach a first paying user.
Put a project guide into practice on Xiaohongshu
Qitian Keaiduo describes someone close to her learning AI image generation from the community and using guides and selected posts to choose products for a Xiaohongshu project.
Use AI to think, as well as to write
Xuexue used AI for copy and summaries. Seeing an approach to analysis in the community prompted her to rethink how AI could help explore a problem, rather than simply finish a task.
From no posts to useful contributions
Chaoji Feng looks back on six months of progress: from writing no content to producing useful posts. The community witnessed a process of regular practice and sharing.
A small group-chat problem can inspire a product
Seeing a member’s chat-backup website, Luuuuke noticed how useful group answers get lost. It inspired an idea for a tool to preserve valuable conversations.
A book club that also discusses work
Aurorabing describes an in-person reading group where members discussed books, content-creation obstacles and managing time as a freelancer, and answered each other’s questions.
A practical starting point for an AI beginner
Guo Xiaowen combines an AI project tutorial for beginners with personal experience. Read the process before choosing your own first step.
Exploring freelance work after a layoff
Xuxu looks back on moving from programming to freelance work. Her account offers another work path to explore when considering a career change.
How a freelancer uses the community
Liangchenmei’s guide for new members introduces Shengcai through personal experience as an independent entrepreneur and freelancer.
Learn with people who put ideas into practice
After three years, Fafa sees an evolving resource library and people who learn by doing. She has collected her experience in a guide for new members.
Validate an idea, then build a repeatable process
Kanshao2077’s reflections emphasize action: test market and user needs first, then turn what works into templates, products and repeatable workflows.
You do not need to study every project. Choose a direction close to your knowledge, skills or available time; read one resource and test one small idea.
